title: Phase-aware hybrid quota + deadline prefill-decode scheduler
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: The current prefill/decode scheduler achieves good average throughput but struggles to meet tail latency SLOs for latency-sensitive traffic and can exhibit token-starvation for low-RT requests when a small number of large batched prefill jobs dominate the queue. Existing approaches (fairshare, phase-splitting) each trade either latency or throughput.

Proposal: Implement a phase-aware hybrid scheduler that: (1) splits work into explicit phases (PREFILL and DECODE) to enable phase-specific admission and batching policies; (2) combines a per-phase quota system for fair resource allocation with per-request soft-deadlines for latency-sensitive requests; and (3) uses token-aging weights and dynamic quota redistribution to avoid starvation. The scheduler will be kernel-aware: it annotates requests with expected kernel/memory profiles (long-context vs short-context, kv-cache warm vs cold) so the runtime can prefer compatible co-batching and reduce kernel switches.

Goals: decrease 99th percentile latency for small-chat requests by >=30% under mixed workloads, keep throughput degradation <10% for batch-heavy inference, and eliminate multi-minute starvation incidents observed in production traces.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler runs behind a feature flag and can be toggled per-customer
99p latency for 8-token chat requests reduced by >=30% on mixed production-like workload (A/B)
End-to-end throughput drop for throughput-only synthetic workloads <10%
No regression in per-token cost beyond expected small variance (<5%)
Scheduler emits metrics: per-phase queue length, deadline misses, quota preemption events, kernel-switch counts
implementation_plan: Design phase: finalize policy math for quotas+deadlines and token-aging weights (this doc)
Prototype: implement phase-split queue and deadline scoring inside scheduler loop (inference-scheduler service)
Kernel hints: add lightweight request annotation for kernel profile and pass through to runtime (serving-agent)
Admission control: implement soft-deadline preemption with bounded rollbacks and fallback to coarser model variant
Testing: unit tests for fairness invariants, integration tests with local runtime + mock GPU kernels
Benchmarking: run distributed A/B against canary traffic and synthetic mixes (50/50 small chats vs large prefill batches)
Rollout: opt-in in canary region -> global gradual ramp -> enabled-by-default for P50 customers after 6 weeks
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal dogfood on staging with synthetic mixes; collect metrics and refine quota params
Week 2: enable for 5% of production requests (non-critical customers) behind flag; run canary dashboards
Week 3-4: increase to 25%/50% evaluating latency and throughput tradeoffs; tune token-aging half-life and deadline multipliers
Week 5: open PR for config defaults and observability; begin gradual global enable for new customers
Week 6-8: monitor, rollback guardrails in place; post-mortem if regressions
benchmarks_expected: Mixed workload (60% small chat, 40% large prefill): reduce 99p latency for small chat by 30%
Throughput-only workload (prefill-heavy): <10% throughput loss; kernel switch count reduced by >15% when kernel hints are accurate
Deadline-aware traffic: deadline miss rate <1% for requests tagged "latency-sensitive"
updates: 2025-02-12 - Created ticket and initial design writeup (Sofia)
2025-02-18 - Prototype PoC shows 22% 99p improvement on local bench (Marcus). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
2025-02-25 - Observability hooks added: per-phase histograms and quota-utilization meter. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/311
2025-03-01 - Found starvation corner-case when many long-prefill tasks with identical quotas lock decode slots; introduced token-aging + soft-preemption to prototype
2025-03-04 - Integration test added for kernel-hint propagation; performance still sensitive to hint accuracy. Next: add lightweight hint calibration step and fallbacks
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: kernel-hints inaccurate -> decreased co-batching efficiency. Mitigation: conservative hinting with runtime feedback loop and automatic fallback to legacy batching policy

Risk: deadline preemption causes thrashing and wasted compute. Mitigation: soft deadlines that mark a request for prioritized scheduling rather than immediate eviction; allow bounded checkpoint rollback for prefill work

Risk: complexity increase in scheduler leading to regressions. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, extensive unit/integration tests, and a simple fail-open path that reverts to existing fairshare policy
open_questions: What should be the default token-aging half-life for mixed production workloads? (start with 30s as a hypothesis)
How to encode kernel profile hints with minimal overhead? (options: histogram-based labels, single enum, or numeric cost estimate)
Should deadline tags be exposed in the public API or only used internally via routing/priority headers?
notes: This ticket coordinates closely with ENG-20458 (token-slice priority) and ENG-9270 (adaptive prefill-decode scheduler). Aim to keep the new scheduler composable so parts can be backported as feature toggles.
design_notes: Prefer simple, auditable scoring function: score = base_priority + deadline_boost - (age_weight * token_count_age) + kernel_alignment_bonus. Keep constants configurable via console for rapid tuning.
